answer.rationale: Temporal correlation is the strongest available signal: the release landed 2h ago and write-path p99 has been climbing 90m, which fits a release-induced regression better than pure load (settlement peak is a recurring, previously-absorbed pattern per memory_b3, and peak alone would not usually produce a monotonic 90m climb to 5x). So rollback_release is my leading direction. But the inherited memory set is uniformly success-flavored — every record is a win story with no failure or no-op cases — so it is survivorship-biased and cannot tell me base rates or applicability boundaries. I therefore spend the budget on the two records that most directly bear on the decision. memory_b1 is the rollback precedent, but as consolidated it describes a checkout ERROR spike, not a write-path LATENCY climb, and says nothing about whether the rollback ran under peak write load; I need the original record to know if the analogy holds and whether the prior build's schema/data path was actually backward-compatible. memory_b5 is the only competing memory that explicitly claims transactional WRITE latency recovery, so it is the strongest non-rollback hypothesis and worth checking whether the mechanism (primary contention from read load) plausibly matches today's symptom. I did not verify memory_b2 (failover) or memory_b4 (circuit breaker) because both risk exactly what the objective forbids: failover mid-peak-settlement can strand or duplicate in-flight writes, and a breaker on the write path fails writes fast rather than preserving them. Key risk I am flagging: rolling back during peak settlement is not value-neutral — if the release included a forward-only migration, an irreversible-schema rollback could corrupt or drop customer writes, which is worse than elevated latency. That is why I am committing only to a small_guarded_test: roll back a limited cohort/instance slice first, confirm p99 diverges favorably from the untouched slice, and only then widen. This preserves the ability to abort, and it keeps the single-intervention budget from being spent on an irreversible broad move made on correlational evidence. If verification shows memory_b1 was an error-spike-only case with no write-load overlap, or shows a forward-only migration in the current release, I will switch to route_read_replicas as the reversible pressure-relief option.
